item.title: Quadratic mixing for the Lee--Sidford Dikin walk
item.description: arXiv:2610.22374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K=\{x\in\R^d:Ax\ge b\}$ be a bounded full-dimensional polytope with $m$ inequalities. For targets on $K$ with density proportional to $\exp(-\vartheta^\transpose x)$, we prove a $\widetilde O(d^2)$ bound, measured in Markov chain iterations, for the chi-square mixing of the $1/2$-lazy Metropolis Dikin walk based on a polylogarithmically rescaled Lee--Sidford metric. The estimate holds for every initial law with finite chi-square divergence. The proof controls the reverse Gaussian proposal through a quantitative average self-concordance estimate at the required $O(1/d)$ scale. We establish this estimate from uniform analytic derivative bounds for the Lewis-weight subspace and an all-order projection-weighted contraction inequality for Gaussian chaoses. For order $j$, the latter bounds each base-point polynomial at scale $d^{j/2}$, up to $j$-dependent and logarithmic factors. Truncating at logarithmic order then absorbs the remaining pathwise loss. This resolves, in the affirmative, the open problem of whether the Gaussian Lee--Sidford Dikin walk mixes in $\widetilde O(d^2)$ iterations: the previously stated quadratic bounds \cite[Theorem~1.4]{LLV20}, \cite[Theorem~1.2]{GKM24} rest on reverse-proposal steps identified as unresolved in \cite[Section~1]{Kook26}, whose $\widetilde O(d^{9/4})$ bound was the best rigorously established rate prior to this work. The proof is found by ChatGPT 5.6 Pro.
item.dc:creator: Yiping Lu

item.title: Strict monotonicity of weighted inhomogeneous percolation thresholds under covering maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.22417v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bernoulli bond percolation under weak covering maps for a class of weighted inhomogeneous product measures such that each edge $e$ carries a positive weight $w(e)$ and is open at intensity $\lambda\geq 0$ with probability $1-\exp(-\lambda w(e))$. We prove a strict monotonicity of the weighted critical intensities $\lambda_c$ in the covering compatibility setting under bounded degree, uniform ellipticity, tame fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. While for the weighted uniform connection thresholds $\lambda_{\mathrm{conn}}$, we establish their strict monotonicity for non-injective weak covering maps under bounded degree, covering compatibility, uniform ellipticity, bounded-fibre and disjoint tree-lifting. Moreover, we verify a general-profile theorem on strict monotonicities of the two thresholds $\lambda_c$ and $\lambda_{\mathrm{conn}}$ respectively under explicit compact-interval finite-energy, derivative bounds and aforementioned geometric conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jing Liu, Kainan Xiang, Lang Zou

item.title: The transition between order to disorder in the Sepp\"al\"ainen-Johansson model
item.description: arXiv:2610.22557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Sepp\"al\"ainen-Johansson model of first-passage percolation along a region of the plane where it moves from an ordered to a disordered phase, represented by a 2nd order discontinuity in its limit shape function. The fluctuations in this transition region are of order one, and we determine that certain limiting statistics are described by Fredholm determinants and are closely related to the largest eigenvalue of the GUE.
item.dc:creator: Mustazee Rahman

item.title: Volterra-Skorokhod Reflection and Fluid Limits of Loss Queues
item.description: arXiv:2610.22607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the $G_t/G/n/n$ loss queue, a customer blocked at time $u$ remains missing from the system for as long as it would have been served. A fraction $K(t-u)$ of the blocking at $u$ therefore still affects the occupancy at time $t$, where $K=1-G$ is the service survival function. We show that, for every arrival process satisfying a functional strong law of large numbers, the fluid limit of this queue is a reflection with kernel $K$ of the fluid limit of the associated infinite-server queue. The reflection is defined by a one-sided reflection problem on $(-\infty,1]$ in which the regulator is convolved with a memory kernel. Given a c\`adl\`ag input $\rho$ and a kernel $K$ with $K(0)=1$, we seek a pair $(\hat\rho,\eta)$ such that $\hat\rho=\rho-\int_0^\cdot K(\cdot-u)\,d\eta(u)$ takes values in $(-\infty,1]$, $\eta$ is nondecreasing, and $\eta$ increases only when $\hat\rho=1$. We refer to this problem as the Volterra-Skorokhod problem. We show existence and uniqueness of the solution and that the solution map is Lipschitz continuous in the uniform norm and nonanticipating. It therefore applies to stochastic inputs path by path. Unlike the classical Skorokhod map, this map is not monotone. For nonincreasing kernels, however, the regulator is the smallest admissible one and monotone in the input. In the queue, this orders the cumulative fluid losses under ordered arrival rates. Furthermore, since arrivals enter the queue through the reflection kernel, the regulator is a thinning of the arrivals.
item.dc:creator: Mingrui Wang, Prakash Chakraborty

item.title: Singular vectors of sparse random rectangular matrices: Transition between delocalized and semilocalized phases
item.description: arXiv:2610.22658v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider the bipartite Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graph $\mathbb{G}(n,m,d/\sqrt{mn})$ at the critical sparsity $d = b\log(N)$ for some $b > 0$ with $N = n + m$, and constant aspect ratio $\gamma = n/m \geq 1$. We show that the spectrum of its centered and rescaled bi-adjacency matrix, whose limiting law is the Mar\v{c}enko--Pastur (MP) distribution, is split into two phases: in the bulk, singular vectors are completely delocalized, while near the edges, singular vectors are semilocalized, with their mass concentrating on small disjoint balls, centered at vertices with extreme degrees. As $b$ decreases, we identify sharp thresholds for the emergence of outlier singular values. For explicit $b_{\rm R}^{\star}$ and $b_{\rm L}^{\star}$ as functions of $\gamma$, we prove that when $b > b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, there is no outlier outside the bulk; when $b_{\rm L}^{\star}< b < b_{\rm R}^{\star}$, only right outliers emerge; and when $b < b_{\rm L}^{\star}$, outliers are present on both sides, all with high probability. This removes an extra technical condition from our previous work arxiv:2508.01456, providing a complete characterization of the parameter space. In sparser regimes, in terms of left outliers, we provide some nontrivial generating mechanisms, demonstrating that local graph structure plays a key role in understanding extreme singular values. Our proofs rely on two technical inputs: (1) an entrywise local law in the MP bulk, where the deterministic equivalent of the resolvent depends on both variance profiles and normalized vertex degrees, different from the Gaussian setting; (2) spectral radius upper bounds for nonbacktracking matrices constructed from regularized random graphs, recently developed in arXiv: 2609.26615. Our results reveal fruitful phenomena for sparse random rectangular matrices at criticality, which are beyond the universality class of their Gaussian counterparts.
item.dc:creator: Ioana Dumitriu, Hai-Xiao Wang

item.title: Normal approximation for total magnetization in subcritical long-range Ising models
item.description: arXiv:2610.22835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Berry--Esseen bounds and 1-Wassershtein bounds for the total spin of strictly subcritical zero-field Ising models with summable interactions. Let $J:\mathbb Z^d\to[0,\infty)$ be symmetric, satisfy $J(0)=0$, and $\|J\|_1:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^d}J(x)<\infty$. For a nonempty finite set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, consider zero-field Gibbs measure with free boundary conditions, in which a spin configuration $\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}^{\Lambda}$ has probability proportional to \[ \exp\!\left\{ \beta\sum_{x,y\in\Lambda} J(x-y)\sigma_x\sigma_y \right\}. \] Let $S_\Lambda:=\sum_{x\in\Lambda}\sigma_x$ be the total spin and $\beta_{\mathrm c}$ denote the critical inverse temperature. For every fixed $0\leq\beta<\beta_{\mathrm c}$, we prove that \[ d_{\mathrm K}\!\left( \frac{S_\Lambda}{\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}(S_\Lambda)}},G \right) \leq C_{\beta,J}|\Lambda|^{-1/2}, \] where $d_{\mathrm K}$ is the Kolmogorov distance, $G\sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, and $C_{\beta,J}$ depends only on $\beta$ and $J$. For the fully periodized model on $(\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z)^d$, the corresponding rate is $L^{-d/2}$, uniformly in $L$. For the classical nearest-neighbor model, the Kolmogorov bound also holds for $-\beta_{\mathrm c}<\beta<\beta_{\mathrm c}$, covering both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic interactions. We also obtain $1$-Wasserstein bounds with the same rates in the respective subcritical regimes. Both the Kolmogorov and $1$-Wasserstein bounds hold with the same rate under the corresponding infinite-volume free-boundary Gibbs measures.
item.dc:creator: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Yang Xie, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: On Niu's Conjecture for Two-Station Tandem Queues
item.description: arXiv:2610.22837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a long standing conjecture in queueing theory made by Niu (1980): in a two-station tandem queueing system with constant service time (c) at station 1, the stationary average waiting time at station 2 is nonincreasing in c. Two very different proofs are provided: one for the general case and one for a special case in which the arrival process is Poisson and the service time at station 2 is exponential.
item.dc:creator: Hao Cao, Jian-Qiang Hu, Qixin Wang

item.title: Sharp asymptotics for the Lov\'asz number of random circulant graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.22971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the LOV\'ASZ number of dense random circulant graphs generated by independent Bernoulli bits indexed by cyclic distances. Although only $O(n)$ independent random inputs determine $O(n^2)$ globally dependent edge indicators, we prove sharp expectation asymptotics along all odd orders, including composite orders, with leading constant one. This resolves a conjecture posed for random circulant graphs in 2025. The proof combines an exact Fourier reduction and complementary duality with a positive interior smoothing that reveals a nonlinear random fixed-point equation. To analyze this equation under the strong dependence of the distance-bit model, we construct canonical tree fields, establish growing-degree Gaussian approximations through polynomial comparison and Wick/Hermite expansions, and transfer the resulting approximation back to the original sign model. A deterministic residual estimate together with an explicit exceptional-event integration yields the sharp expectation asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Xin Chen, Hongwei Hu, Yanqing Hu, Wei Wang, Luzhen Yang

item.title: Perron-Wright asymptotics and critical component processes for regular inhomogeneous random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.23003v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend Wright's enumeration of connected labelled graphs with fixed surplus to irreducible critical finite type kernels and regular compact type kernels. Let $C_t(k,r)$ denote the total weight of connected labelled graphs with $k$ vertices and surplus $r$. Let $u>0$ satisfy $Ku=u$ and $\int u\,d\mu=1$, and put $\alpha=\int u^2\,d\mu$ and $\beta=\int u^3\,d\mu$. We prove that the rooted-tree radius $\rho$ is positive and real analytic near $1$, with $\rho(1)=1$ and $\log\rho(t)=\frac{\alpha^2}{2\beta}(t-1)^2+O(|t-1|^3)$, and that, for fixed $r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and $0\le L < \infty$, $C_t(k,r)=w_r\beta^{(r-1)/2}e^{-k}\rho(t)^{-k}k^{k+3r/2-2}\{1+O_{r,L}(k^{-1/2})\}$, uniformly for $|t-1|\le Lk^{-1/2}$, where $w_r$ is the classical Wright constant. At $t_n=1+\lambda n^{-1/3}$, these asymptotics yield local size and surplus point-process limits for deterministic finite type models and annealed compact type Bollobas-Janson-Riordan models satisfying projective quadratic regularity. After rescaling component sizes by $\beta^{1/3}n^{-2/3}$, the limit is the Aldous process at parameter $\alpha\beta^{-2/3}\lambda$, and the corresponding type profiles concentrate at the Perron law $p(dx)=u(x)\mu(dx)$. For every regular countable critical kernel, we construct graph sequences with growing finite supports and the same local limits, and identify the additive shift of the critical window caused by spectral perturbations of order $n^{-1/3}$.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Hu, Wen Sun

item.title: Regularising Flows and Singular Fractional SDEs with Superlinear Dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study stochastic differential equations driven by the fractional Riemann-Liouville process with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1)$, whose drift is the sum of a possibly distributional vector field $b$ and a smooth, one-sided Lipschitz, dissipative vector field $F$ with coercivity of order $k+1$ and polynomially growing derivatives. If $b \in \mathcal{C}^\gamma(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $\gamma<1$ satisfying $\gamma>\max\{1-1/(2H),2-1/H\}$, and if $H+1/(k-1)>(1-\gamma)H/2$, we construct a solution by smooth approximation and prove uniqueness in a class defined through local comparison with the flow generated by the dissipative drift. We also establish quantitative temporal regularity and stability estimates. The proof combines a conditional decomposition of fractional Brownian motion, Malliavin integration by parts, uniform non-degeneracy estimates for the regularising flow, and the stochastic sewing lemma.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Dareiotis, El Mehdi Haress, Khoa L\^e

item.title: Nonconvex Carnot Limit Shapes for Branching Random Walks on the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.23162v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a supercritical branching random walk on the discrete Heisenberg group driven by the four standard horizontal generators. Horizontal position has scale $n$, whereas the central coordinate records discrete area and has scale $n^2$. On the Galton-Watson survival event, we prove almost sure Hausdorff convergence, under Carnot scaling, of both the rescaled particle positions and the collections of enhanced ancestral paths. The path limit consists of area lifts of horizontal paths $\omega$ satisfying $J_t(\omega)\le t\log\rho$ for every $t\in[0,1]$, where $\rho$ is the offspring mean. In contrast to the classical Euclidean case, the deterministic limit shape is nonconvex for every $\rho>1$. We identify its horizontal projection and interval vertical fibers, determine the saturated shape for $\rho\ge4$, and characterize the origin fiber below saturation by Wulff duality. A hyperbolic representation gives an elliptic integral formula for the Wulff area. The maximal central coordinate $\Gamma_\rho$ is nondecreasing and concave in $\rho$, equals $1/4$ for $\rho\ge4$, and satisfies $\Gamma_\rho=(\log\rho)/\pi-(\log\rho)^2/(4\pi) +O((\log\rho)^3)$ as $\rho\downarrow1$. For fixed $1<\rho<4$, we obtain $M_n^Z=\Gamma_\rho n^2+O(n^{3/2}\sqrt{\log n})$ almost surely. Above saturation the first correction is a random linear term; at $\rho=4$, under a finite second moment assumption, the deficit $\Gamma_4n^2-M_n^Z$ has order $n\log\log n$ in probability.
item.dc:creator: Bohan Hu, Jungang Li, Wen Sun

item.title: Uniform transport processes and the Brownian sheet:the one-parameter rate of convergence is preserved
item.description: arXiv:2610.23347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In~\cite{BFR} we constructed processes $W_n$, built from a family of independent standard Poisson processes, that converge almost surely to the Brownian sheet uniformly on $[0,1]^2$, and in~\cite{Rov} we proved that $P(\max_{[0,1]^2}|W_n-W|>\alpha n^{-\beta})=o(n^{-q})$ for every $\beta<\lambda/2$, where $\lambda\in(0,\tfrac{1}{5})$ is the parameter of the construction; this gives rates $n^{-\beta}$ with $\beta<\tfrac{1}{10}$. In this paper, we show that the same construction, with $\lambda\geq 1$, satisfies \[ P\!\left(\max_{(s,t)\in[0,1]^2} |W_n(s,t)-W(s,t)| > \alpha\, n^{-1/2}(\log n)^3\right) = o(n^{-q}) \quad\text{for every }q>0, \] which is the one-parameter rate of Gorostiza and Griego~\cite{GG} up to a factor $(\log n)^{1/2}$. In particular the restriction $\lambda<\tfrac{1}{5}$ is not needed.
item.dc:creator: Carles Rovira

item.title: Fluctuations of the planar random walk sausage
item.dc:creator: Maxence Baccara, Joelle Ishak

item.title: On the relation between transformations of SDEs and of associated Kolmogorov equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.23482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The relationship between transformations of one-dimensional stochastic differential equations and those of the associated Kolmogorov backward equations is investigated. Stochastic transformations combining deterministic time changes, space-time diffeomorphisms, and Girsanov-type changes of probability measure are shown to be in correspondence with admissible transformations of the associated linear parabolic equations, namely the transformations preserving the parabolic structure up to the possible introduction of a zero-order potential term. A distinguished subclass of transformations, characterized by the absence of any potential term in the transformed Kolmogorov equation, is shown to coincide exactly with Doob transformations of the underlying probability measure of the SDE. This characterization further establishes a correspondence between Doob symmetries of an SDE and Lie point symmetries of the associated Kolmogorov backward equation. This correspondence, in turn, yields a constructive (probabilistic) Lie symmetry classification of autonomous Kolmogorov backward equations.
item.dc:creator: Susanna Deh\`o, Francesco Carlo De Vecchi, Paola Morando, Stefania Ugolini

item.title: On conservativity of multitype continuous-state branching processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In [4], Grey gives a condition on the branching mechanism $\psi$ of a continuous- state branching process Z ensuring that the process is conservative. This condition is obtained from the expression of the solution of the differential equation satisfied by the Laplace exponent of Z. In higher dimensions, it is generally no longer possible to make this solution explicit and very few conditions ensuring the conservativity of the process are known. In this paper, we provide necessary conditions and sufficient conditions for conservativity. For dimension 2, when types cannot regenerate themselves, we give a necessary and sufficient condition and we invert the Lamperti representation of the multitype branching process.
item.dc:creator: Lo\"{\i}c Chaumont, Cl\'ement Lamoureux

item.title: Random Sampling of Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the effect of random sampling on stochastic processes whose finite-dimensional distributions are Bohr almost periodic under time shifts. The sampling times are generated independently by a two-sided random walk with positive increments or by a two-sided subordinator. Under a non-degeneracy condition we show that the shifted finite-dimensional distributions of the sampled process converge to those of a strictly stationary process. Consequently, if the sampled process is itself almost periodic in distribution, then it must already be strictly stationary. We further prove an $L^2$-law of large numbers for sampled averages under covariance decay and a uniform second-moment bound, and identify its limit with the mean of the stationary limit process. Finally, for $m$-dependent, $L^2$-uniformly integrable almost periodic processes, we establish a central limit theorem for the centered sampled sums, whose asymptotic variance is given by the autocovariance series of the stationary limit.
item.dc:creator: David Berger, Maximilian Strobel

item.title: Higher-order sum rules for zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function
item.description: arXiv:2610.23697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish marginal sum rules for the truncated correlation functions of zeros of the planar Gaussian entire function (GEF). For each fixed integer $k\ge2$, the integral in one coordinate converges absolutely and equals $-(k-1)$ times the truncated correlation of order $k-1$. This answers the marginal-identity question posed by Krishnapur and Yogeshwaran for the planar GEF. We also prove a criterion for simple point processes under local moment and absolute integrability assumptions. Suppose there is a sequence of compactly supported cutoffs between zero and one that are eventually equal to one on each compact set. If the variances of their linear statistics tend to zero, the marginal identities hold almost everywhere. Strong clustering and variance bounds for smooth linear statistics verify these assumptions for GEF zeros. The proof uses mixed cumulants and the partition formula relating ordinary and factorial cumulants.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolin Zhu, Feng Guo

item.title: Universality of Annealed Complexity in the Spherical Pure $p$-Spin Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.23701v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In an influential work, Auffinger, Ben Arous, and \v{C}ern\'y (2013) investigated the limiting annealed complexity in the spherical pure $p$-spin model associated to the Gaussian disorder. Their results, in particular, included an explicit expression for the total number of critical points of the Hamiltonian below any given energy level. In this paper, we consider the same anneal complexity associated to a disorder interpolating between an arbitrary random variable and its Gaussian counterpart. Assuming strict subgaussianity of the former, our result shows that the annealed complexity shares the same limit as in the Gaussian case.
item.dc:creator: Wei-Kuo Chen, Te-Lun Lu, Arnab Sen

item.title: Rapid mixing within a phase for Ising models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23777v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Glauber dynamics for Ising measures conditioned to have a sufficiently large majority of $+1$ spins. Under a sparse spectral width condition on the interaction matrix, we derive a Poincar\'{e} inequality for the conditioned measures from a magnetization drift condition, and a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality from a stronger, entropy weighted condition. As applications, we obtain approximate posterior sampling in total variation distance for $\mathbb{Z}_2$ synchronization at high enough signal-to-noise ratio using $O(n\log n)$ Glauber updates from a spectral initialization. For ferromagnetic Ising models on random $d$-regular graphs, we prove rapid phase ordering down to inverse temperatures of order $1/d$, extending the temperature range of Gheissari, Sly, and Sohn (2025). Finally, we extend these inequalities to unconditioned Ising measures under an inward drift condition outside the conditioned region. This yields $O(n\log n)$ mixing of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every fixed inverse temperature when the external field is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Vasyl Paliy, Youngtak Sohn

item.title: A Universal Lower Bound for the Complexity of Gaussian-Divisible Spin Glasses
item.description: arXiv:2610.23823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a variant of the spherical mixed spin glass model with non-Gaussian disorder. Specifically, we replace the usual standard Gaussian interaction coefficients with Gaussian-divisible ones, meaning that each coefficient can be expressed as the sum of a standard Gaussian random variable and an independent, non-Gaussian random variable. We show that the annealed complexity of this model is at least the annealed complexity of the standard Gaussian model, if the non-Gaussian part is centered and subexponential.
item.dc:creator: Pax Kivimae, Benjamin McKenna

item.title: Analyticity of the correlation length in subcritical FK-percolation and Potts models
item.description: arXiv:2610.23843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the correlation length of FK-percolation and Potts models on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is analytic in the whole subcritical regime of parameters. Our proof makes use of the identification of the polar dual of the mass with the solution of an equation involving the leading eigenvalue of the FK--Ruelle operator, introduced in the context of Ornstein--Zernike theory in Campanino, Ioffe and Velenik (Probab. Theory Relat. Fields, 2003), and crucially relies on Kato's theory of analytic perturbation of linear operators. As a consequence of this result, we prove that the correlation length cannot be invariant by rotation except at countably many values of the temperature parameter in the subcritical phase.
item.dc:creator: Lucas D'Alimonte, Lo\"ic Gassmann

item.title: Space-filling curves and small-ball probabilities for the Kloosterman process
item.description: arXiv:2610.22645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct explicitly a space-filling curve in the support of the limiting Kloosterman process, using the planar partial-sum curve of the Rudin--Shapiro sequence. The qualitative existence statement was previously attributed to J. Bober by Kowalski. The resulting curve is a closed, $1/2$-H\"older continuous loop whose image contains a specified triangle of area $1/128$. Its Fourier coefficients are purely imaginary and satisfy $|\widehat f(h)|\leq(2\pi|h|)^{-1}$ for $h\ne 0$. We also prove a uniform lower bound for small balls centred at closed $1/2$-H\"older curves with a fixed coefficient bound, of the form $\exp\{-C\varepsilon^{-2}\log^2(2/\varepsilon)\}$. Known functional convergence then gives a quantitative lower bound for the limiting proportion of two-parameter Kloosterman paths approximating the constructed loop.
item.dc:creator: Danyil Kyselov

item.title: Poisson-Dirichlet statistics for the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.22821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For $T > 0$ large, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$ and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. For the Riemann zeta function $\zeta$, we study the Gibbs measure with density proportional to $|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|^{\beta}$ on $I_{\theta} := [ - (\log{T})^{\theta},(\log{T})^{\theta}]$, for every $\theta > 0$ and $\beta > 0$. As $\beta$ increases, the Gibbs measure increasingly favors positions where $|\zeta|$ is large, providing a way to study the spatial organization of extreme values. Under explicit conditions on the rate at which $\sigma$ approaches the critical line, a phase transition is established at the critical inverse temperature $\beta_{c}(\theta) := 2\sqrt{1 + \theta}$. The limiting distribution of the correlation (or overlap) between the field values at two positions sampled from the Gibbs measure is concentrated at $0$ when $\beta \leq \beta_{c}(\theta)$, and assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $0$ and $1$, respectively, when $\beta > \beta_{c}(\theta)$. Joint convergence of the overlaps is also established, with the limiting arrays described by Poisson-Dirichlet weights in the low-temperature regime. The Ghirlanda-Guerra identities, which provide recursive relations for the joint overlap distributions, are established in the limit, uniformly for bounded deterministic observables of the sampled positions. All our results are established independently of the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: Stochastic Shockwave Dynamics in First-Order Traffic Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.23022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Moving congestion fronts vary across realizations even when the traffic-flow law is fixed. This paper develops a generator-based formulation of the Lighthill--Whitham--Richards (LWR) model with random initial density and a deterministic fundamental diagram. Randomness enters through the initial spatial density field; every realization follows the same conservation law. For a smooth strictly concave fundamental diagram, we adapt established one-sided spatial Markov closure to traffic variables under the stated spatial-process and regularity assumptions, and derive a kinetic balance for physically normalized front intensities. Evolving the spatial generator provides density laws and congestion-front statistics without solving a road-grid problem for every realization. The formulation is continuous in physical space and time, while its numerical implementation approximates density state and integrates physical time. Four experiments distinguish deterministic consistency from stochastic comparison. Riemann and signal examples recover independently constructed exact LWR solutions. Smooth strictly concave approximations approach the deterministic triangular-diagram signal solution over the tested finite horizons; this does not establish stochastic closure at contacts or the capacity kink. A matched Monte Carlo Godunov ensemble evaluates front counts, sizes, mergers, and density distributions. The evolved generator also yields an instantaneous travel-time distribution for a frozen density field, compared with the same functional of the matched Godunov profiles. This quantity is not experienced travel time through evolving traffic. Resolution checks identify remaining normalization and small-front-loss effects. The contribution is direct evolution and interpretation of traffic-state and front distributions under a fixed first-order traffic law.
item.dc:creator: Yanlin Zhang, Alireza Talebpour

item.title: Singular Stochastic Heat Equations with Fractional Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.23189v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the paracontrolled distribution approach of Gubinelli, Imkeller, and Perkowski to singular stochastic heat equations with Caputo fractional time derivatives. By establishing Schauder estimates for the time-fractional heat flow and controlling history terms, we address the difficulties arising from temporal memory and the lack of the semigroup property. For the one-dimensional rough Burgers-type equation driven by space-time white noise with spatial dissipation \((-\Delta)^\sigma\), we prove global well-posedness for \(\sigma\in(5/6,1]\) and \(\nu\in(6\sigma/(12\sigma-5),1]\). For the heat equation with nonlinear multiplicative spatial white noise on the two-dimensional torus, we establish local well-posedness of renormalized solutions and an \(L^\infty\) blow-up criterion for every \(\nu\in(0,1]\).
item.dc:creator: Shuolin Zhang, \quad Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Rough Stochastic Viscous Camassa-Holm equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.23198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish well-posedness results for the viscous Camassa--Holm equation driven by the additive Gaussian noise $(1-\partial_x^2)^{-\eta}\xi$, where $\xi$ denotes the space-time white noise and $\eta>-1/12$. This formulation includes spatially colored noise for $\eta>0$, space-time white noise for $\eta=0$, and rough noise for $-1/12<\eta<0$. More precisely, we establish a pathwise solution theory via approximation by equations driven by regularized noises. The main difficulty arises from the singular interactions between the nonlinear terms and the irregular stochastic convolution. By introducing suitable enhanced stochastic objects and applying paracontrolled techniques, we obtain local well-posedness for the full range $\eta>-1/12$. Furthermore, when $\eta>1/4$, we establish global well-posedness by deriving suitable energy estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoxin Chen, Yiyao Lian, Zhaoyang Yin, Shuolin Zhang

item.title: Emergence of Correlations Between Records and Maximum in Random Time Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.23217v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute exactly the covariance between the maximum $M$ and the number of records $K$ in a discrete time series of $n$ entries as a quantitative probe of the history leading to an extreme event. For continuous IID series, with a common probability distribution function (PDF) $p(x)$, we find the striking result that $M$ and $K$ are uncorrelated for any $n \geq 1$. We show that this independence is rather fragile and the covariance $C_q(n)$ between $M$ and $K$ becomes nonzero when $p(x)$ becomes discontinuous due to a delta-component at $x=0$ with an amplitude $0< q < 1$. This time series models the occurrence of dry days with probability $q$ in a precipitation time series when there is no rainfall. We show that there is an interesting shape transition at a critical value $q_c$ where the covariance $C_q(n)$, as a function of $n$, changes from monotonic ($q<q_c$) to non monotonic behavior (for $q>q_c$). We compute the critical strength $q_c$ exactly. Furthermore, for large $n$, we show that $C_q(n)$ decays as a power law, with an exponent that depends on the tail of $p(x)$. We then compare our theoretical predictions with real precipitation data from several weather stations across Germany, finding a very good agreement.
item.dc:creator: Satya N. Majumdar, Sanjib Sabhapandit, Gregory Schehr

item.title: On the skew-curvature power law relationship in a stochastic volatility model with infinite variation L\'evy jumps
item.description: arXiv:2610.23488v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The short-term blow up behaviour of the ATM-IV skew is commonly modelled by either a rough volatility process with small Hurst index or an infinite variation L\'evy process in the log-price dynamics. In this paper, we examine which is the effect of mixed dynamics (i.e. rough volatility and infinite variation L\'evy processes) on the ATM-IV skew and curvature. The results of the paper show that the analysis of the leading terms of the short-time expansion of both ATM-IV skew and curvature allow us to determine, from a mixed dynamics model, which mechanism originates the power-law behaviour on the skew and on the curvature. Apart from showing that the mixed model also originates a power law, it has also key implications in model design and calibration. Numerical evidences for the rough Heston model with CGMY L\'evy jumps are provided.
item.dc:creator: \`Oscar Bur\'es, Josep Vives

item.title: Gaussian measures under the Navier-Stokes and heat flows are mutually singular
item.description: arXiv:2610.23591v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations on the torus $\mathbb{T}^d$, $d \ge 2$, with translation invariant Gaussian random initial data. We show that, for the Gaussian measure formally given by $\mu_0 \sim \exp(-\frac12 \| u \|_{\dot H^\alpha}^2)$ on divergence-free fields, its nonlinear evolution $\nu_t$ and its linear evolution $\mu_t$ are mutually singular for almost every time. Moreover, the same holds for the nonlinear evolution of an arbitrary initial measure $\nu_0$. This is in sharp contrast to the available results for Hamiltonian PDEs, where Gaussian measures are commonly quasi-invariant. We achieve this by showing that there exists a set $\mathscr G_t$ such that $\mu_t(\mathscr G_t) = 1$, but for any smooth solution of Navier-Stokes, the set of times $t$ such that $u(t) \in \mathscr G_t$ is null, which we deduce from a quantitative convexity bound for frequency-localised versions of the (typically infinite) quantity $\| \mathrm{e}^{-t \Delta} u(t) \|_{L^2}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Niko Nikov, Leonardo Tolomeo

item.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
item.description: arXiv:2610.23684v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points. Equivalently, skeletons of a given degree are finite C_2-sets over the C_2-monoid (R,+), these data are their marks, and the semiring is an infinite-monoid analogue of a crossed Burnside semiring. The multiplicative monoid is not cancellative, the only obstruction being that multiplication by a skeleton without fixed points forgets the fixed points; accordingly, the Grothendieck ring has explicit zero divisors. A continuous family of semiring characters, with the degree and the number of fixed points, is a complete invariant, and for commensurable ratios the multiplicative Grothendieck group is described by P\'olya's theorem. The main subject is factorization. The reduced monoid is atomic with bounded lengths, but factorization is not unique, the elasticity is infinite, and even the divisor-closed submonoid with one fixed point is not half-factorial. Without fixed points, every reducible skeleton splits off a single orbit, which gives a criterion by centers, exactly when the number of orbits is 8, 16, a prime or twice a prime. Irreducibility is generic in almost every type. Progression skeletons factor according to mixed-radix number systems, with all factorizations of equal length. Finally, orbit counting gives the dimension of the separatrix and the response rank of products.
item.dc:creator: Juan Antonio Vega Coso

item.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.23695v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator. For weighted scalar-valued functions on facets, the ROL decomposition becomes the law of total variance, recovering classical spectral-gap bounds from local link expansion (Alev and Lau, STOC 2020). Moreover, for positive binary spin distributions, conditional influence describes the overlap of the corresponding subspaces, yielding known heat-bath gap bounds from spectral independence (Anari, Liu, and Oveis Gharan, FOCS 2020). The framework also offers a route toward quantum Gibbs sampling, with applications requiring model-specific geometric estimates and energy comparisons.
item.dc:creator: Ryu Hayakawa

item.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.23775v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give faster algorithms for sampling from the uniform distribution over a polytope. Our main result is an algorithm that, when applied to a polytope with $m$ constraints in $n$ dimensions, uses $m \cdot \mathrm{poly}\log(\frac m \delta)$ iterations, each running in time $O(mn^{\omega - 1})$, to return a sample within total variation distance $\delta$ to the uniform distribution. When $m =O(n)$ and $\delta = \mathrm{poly}(\frac 1 n)$, our runtime improves upon all prior works by an $\Omega(n^{2/3})$ factor. Our sampler is based on the recent \emph{functional stochastic localization} framework of [GST26], and achieves an iteration count nearly matching the Poincar\'e constant of the uniform distribution with respect to the logarithmic barrier.
item.dc:creator: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian, Hubert Yang

item.title: Thin-thick approach to martingale representations on progressively enlarged filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2406.08983v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the predictable representation property in the progressive enlargement F^\tau of a reference filtration F by a random time \tau. Our approach is based on the decomposition of any random time into two parts, one overlapping F-stopping times (thin part) and the other one that avoids F-stopping times (thick part). We assume that the F-thin part of \tau is nontrivial and prove a martingale representation theorem on F^\tau. We thus extend previous results dealing with F-avoiding random times. We collect some examples of application to the enlargement of the natural filtration of a L\'evy process.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance (2026)
item.dc:creator: Antonella Calzolari (Department of Mathematics - University of Rome "Tor Vergata'', Rome, Italy), Barbara Torti (Department of Mathematics - University of Rome "Tor Vergata'', Rome, Italy)

item.title: Singularity and regularity of the critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow
item.description: arXiv:2504.06128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) provides a natural candidate solution to the ill-posed 2D Stochastic Heat Equation with multiplicative space-time white noise. In this paper, we initiate the investigation of the spatial properties of the SHF. We prove that, as a random measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$, it is a.s. singular w.r.t. the Lebesgue measure. This is obtained by probing a "quasi-critical" regime and showing the asymptotic log-normality of the mass assigned to vanishing balls, as the disorder strength is sent to zero at a suitable rate, accompanied by similar results for critical 2D directed polymers. We also describe the regularity of the SHF, showing that it is a.s. H\"older $C^{-\epsilon}$ for any $\epsilon>0$, implying the absence of atoms, and we establish local convergence to zero in the long time limit.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Caravenna, Rongfeng Sun, Nikos Zygouras

item.title: On the pair correlation function of the Sine$_\beta$ process
item.description: arXiv:2509.15446v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Sine$_\beta$ process, the bulk point process scaling limit of beta-ensembles. We provide a representation of its pair correlation function for all $\beta>0$ via a stochastic differential equation, and also via an infinite system of differential equations. We show that the pair correlation function is continuous in $\beta$, and provide estimates for its asymptotic decay. When $\beta=2n$ is an even integer, we characterize the pair correlation function through a linear system of $n$ ordinary differential equations and derive the function's power series expansion. Our results recover the classical explicit formula for the pair correlation function in the $\beta=2$ and $4$ cases. We obtain our results by studying the one-point function of the $\operatorname{HP}_{\beta,\delta}$ process, the point process limit of the circular Jacobi beta-ensemble.
item.dc:creator: Yahui Qu, Benedek Valk\'o

item.title: On the depth of depth-weighted trees
item.description: arXiv:2602.15709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The depth-weighted tree DWT($f$) with weight function $f:\{0,1,2,\ldots\}\to (0,\infty)$ is a dynamic random tree grown from a root $r$ where vertices arrive consecutively and every new vertex attaches to a parent $u$ with probability proportional to $f$(distance between $u$ and $r$). This work is dedicated to a systematic analysis of the depth of DWT($f$). Namely, we provide precise analytic expressions of the typical depth of DWT($f$) for convergent, periodic, slowly growing, and (super-)exponentially growing weight functions. Furthermore, for bounded or exponentially growing $f$, we determine the typical depth up to a multiplicative constant, thus confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Leckey, Mitsche and Wormald.
item.dc:creator: Lyuben Lichev, Amitai Linker, Bas Lodewijks, Dieter Mitsche

item.title: The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape
item.description: arXiv:2605.21366v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the directed landscape, the Martin boundary coincides with the horofunction boundary. We show that functions in this boundary are precisely the eternal solutions possessing a spatial growth rate, and that the minimal Martin boundary is given by the Busemann functions. Moreover, every eternal solution can be expressed as a max-plus convex combination of countably many Busemann functions. Horofunctions are exactly those eternal solutions that admit a representation in terms of at most two Busemann functions with a common growth rate. As a consequence of instability, not all horofunctions are Busemann functions, and the Martin boundary is strictly larger than its minimal part.
item.dc:creator: Firas Rassoul-Agha, Mikhail Sweeney

item.title: Multilevel limits of spiked random matrix corners processes
item.description: arXiv:2608.01531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the largest eigenvalues of submatrices of the classical Gaussian random matrices with a finite rank spike in the critical BBP regime. We show that they converge to a multilevel interlacing particle system whose lowest level is the Airy$_\beta$ point process. Our construction and scaling limits extend in a natural way to non-classical $\beta >0$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Landon, Tara Stojimirovic

item.title: Uniform logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the 2D Coulomb gas at the diffusive temperature scale
item.description: arXiv:2608.24863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $N\ge2$ and $\beta>0$, consider the canonical 2D Coulomb gas ensemble \begin{equation} \mathrm{d}\mathbb{P}_{N,\beta}(Z) =\mathsf{Z}_{N,\beta}^{-1}e^{-\beta|Z|^2/2} \prod_{i<j}|z_i-z_j|^{\beta/N}\mathrm{d} Z \qquad\text{on }\mathbb{C}^N. \end{equation} The factor $N^{-1}$ in the pair exponent places the ensemble at the diffusive, or high-temperature, scale. We prove that, for every fixed inverse temperature $\beta>0$, this Gibbs measure satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality (LSI) on the closed Dirichlet-form domain generated by collision-free compactly supported smooth functions, with a positive constant independent of $N$. The LSI constant may be chosen uniformly when $\beta$ ranges over a compact subset of $(0,\infty)$. A second main result establishes Poincar\'e and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for planar Gaussian measures weighted by finite products of positive powers of distances to points, with constants depending only on the total variance of the underlying Gaussian measure and the total exponent, not on the number or locations of the points. To prove the full labeled Poincar\'e inequality, we decompose variance into permutation-invariant and label-dependent parts, controlled respectively by a weighted $\bar\partial$ estimate and by relative-coordinate conditioning with random transpositions; separately, one-site logarithmic Sobolev inequalities, a conditional entropy inequality, and a repulsive partition estimate give a defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. Rothaus tightening combines the resulting full labeled Poincar\'e inequality with the defective logarithmic Sobolev inequality. The two main theorems on their stated closed form domains and all results used in their formal proofs, including those from the literature, have been formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Rosenzweig

item.title: Differentiability of the Leading Lyapunov Exponent of a linear differential equation with random coefficients Application to the Calculation of the Selection Gradient in Random Environments
item.description: arXiv:2609.02711v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The study of evolution in temporally fluctuating environments often relies on the analysis of Lyapunov exponents, which quantify the exponential growth of populations. However, when model parameters depend on a stochastic process, calculating the selection gradient, a key tool for predicting the evolution of phenotypic traits, becomes a mathematical challenge. While the periodic case has been resolved, a general approach for random environments remains to be developed. This article proposes a rigorous method to: Establish the differentiability of the leading Lyapunov exponent with respect to a parameter, providing an explicit integral formula for its derivative. Develop a numerical algorithm to approximate the derivative by solving an extended differential equation. Apply these results to the analysis of mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, identifying the selection gradient as the derivative of the top Lyapunov exponent.
item.dc:creator: Philippe Carmona

item.title: Critical branching random walks on $\mathbb{Z}^2$: local survival probabilities and Yaglom limit theorems
item.description: arXiv:2609.15538v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a branching random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with critical offspring of mean $1$ and spatial motion governed by the jumps of a lazy simple random walk. For every site $x\in\mathbb{Z}^2$, we obtain a uniform asymptotical estimate for the local survival probability, i.e., the probability that there are particles at $x$ at large time $n$. Using Stein's method, we establish a Yaglom-type theorem for the number of particles at $x$ at time $n$ when $x$ is at distance of order $\sqrt{n}$ from the origin. Moreover, at the position occupied by a typical particle at time $n$, the number of particles at that site, normalized by $\log n$, converges in law to a Gamma distribution, thereby confirming a conjecture of Lalley and Zheng [Ann. Probab. 39 (2010), 327-368]. Finally, we prove that, conditional on local survival, the total number of particles at time $n$, divided by $n$, also converges weakly to a Gamma distribution.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Bai, Xinxin Chen, Shen Lin

item.title: Sharp singularity asymptotics for discrete random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.39463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We resolve the Rademacher singularity conjecture: an $n\times n$ matrix with independent uniform $\{-1,1\}$ entries is singular with probability $(2+o(1))n^22^{-n}$. More generally, for an $n\times n$ matrix $M_n$ with independent entries uniform on a fixed set $S\subset\mathbb{R}$ of cardinality $q\ge2$, we prove $\mathbb{P}(s_n(M_n)\le z/\sqrt{n}) \le Cz+a_n(S)+C'n^{1+\varepsilon}q^{-n}$ for all $n\ge1$, $z\ge0$, and $\varepsilon>0$, with $C=C(S)$ and $C'=C'(S,\varepsilon)$. Here $s_n$ denotes the least singular value, and $a_n(S)$ is the sum of the probabilities of the events involving zero rows or columns and equal or opposite pairs of rows or columns.
item.dc:creator: Xuanang Hu, Zeyan Song, Xinglong Wu

item.title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
item.description: arXiv:2609.39946v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $\Delta V(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{N\Delta V(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we check it against mean extinction times obtained without the action solver, i.e., from the backward equation of the jump process on a truncated lattice and from exact stochastic simulation. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $\Delta V(r)=\Delta V_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $\Delta V_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first, and at $r=1$ the barrier is 55% larger than $\Delta V_\infty$. A formal first-order expansion attributes this increase to the lag of the signal, of which the fluctuations of the signal remove a quarter. The saddle barrier $\Delta V(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, whereas the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply, by paths which keep the signal high and are usually followed by recovery. The mean extinction times of the backward equation, which include failed attempts, have a prefactor which tends to a constant, and they grow at a rate within $10^{-5}$ of $\Delta V(r)$ at every tested rate.
item.dc:creator: Mario Ayala, Johannes Zimmer

item.title: Critical Free-Energy Variance in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.00011v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the variance of the free energy in the Gaussian Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at zero external field. For every system size and inverse temperature $\beta>0$, we prove $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(\beta) \le \log\chi+(\beta^2-1)(\chi-1), \chi=N\mathbb{E}\langle R_{1,2}^2\rangle_\beta$, where $R_{1,2}$ is the replica overlap and $F_N^{\mathrm{off}}=N^{-1}\log Z_N^{\mathrm{off}}$ omits diagonal disorder. The proof uses an exact identity for the edges incident to one spin, Schur complements, and Gaussian disorder interpolation. At criticality the bound reduces to $2N^2\operatorname{Var} F_N^{\mathrm{off}}(1)\le\log\chi$. An explicit nonnegative integral measures its gap. A second decomposition relates this gap to a mixed cubic overlap functional. Existing moment and cavity estimates imply that its required integral is bounded. Critical susceptibility asymptotics give the sharp logarithmic upper coefficient and show that the gap converges exactly when the variance has a constant term. We extend an entropy bound throughout bounded critical temperature windows and establish overlap moment stability on a smaller interval.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Tierz

item.title: DisCo Algebra: Why Disintegration and Combination Are Not Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.15006v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present DisCo algebra---a compositional framework for joint probability built from a symmetric cooperad (disintegration) and a non-unital partial symmetric operad (combination restricted to the image of disintegration) on the bare family $\mathcal{P}_n=\mathrm{Prob}([0,1]^n)$. No probability integral transform, no external summary functions, no enrichment of objects with conditional kernels. The disintegration side uses block-wise joint CDFs as intrinsic, measure-determined 1D summaries, yielding a lossy compression. The combination side reads the same summaries and reconstructs via regular conditional measures, yielding a lossless embedding on admissible inputs. We prove that combination followed by disintegration is the identity on admissible inputs, but disintegration followed by combination is not---it defines a renormalization operator $R_{\mathcal{I}}=\text{Combine}\circ\text{Disintegrate}$. The information loss of this operator is exactly the probability curvature $\mathcal{K}_{\mathcal{I}}(\mu)$---the conditional KL divergence between the true conditional distribution and the conditionally independent product. This curvature measures the obstruction to lossless decomposition and reveals a hard limit on how much cross-block dependence can be captured by CDF-based scalar block summaries.
item.dc:creator: Xuexing Lu

item.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.18353v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{\xi_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{\xi_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^{\alpha}}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha>-1/2 $ is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Li-Xin Zhang

item.title: Exact Endpoint Asymptotics and Almost-Sure Limits for Uniform Empirical Measures in Two Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the empirical measure of the first $n$ points of one infinite sequence of independent uniform samples in the unit square, we identify the leading constant in the bounded-Lipschitz distance to area measure, equivalently in $W_1$, both in expectation and almost surely along all sample sizes. The constant is $c_*=\kappa_1/(2\sqrt\pi)\in(0,1/4]$, where $\kappa_1$ is the linear-growth Gaussian variational constant of Armegioiu--Goldman--Grotto--Trevisan. This answers the two-dimensional bounded-Lipschitz convergence question posed by Yukich in 1989. We give the complete endpoint argument, square--torus comparison, empirical reduction, and full-sequence probability argument.
item.dc:creator: Weitao Huang, Renzhen Wang, Yichen Wu, Deyu Meng

item.title: Optimal estimates for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of deep random ReLU neural networks
item.description: arXiv:2506.19695v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper studies the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants of ReLU neural networks $\Phi: \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$ with random parameters for $p \in [1,\infty]$. The distribution of the weights follows a variant of the He initialization. In the case of zero-bias networks, we derive matching high-probability upper and lower bounds for wide networks that differ at most by an absolute constant. The bounds reveal two remarkable phenomena. First, the bounds grow root-logarithmically in terms of the depth of the net. Second, the behavior of the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants varies significantly between the regimes $p \in [1,2)$ and $p \in [2,\infty]$. For $p \in [2,\infty]$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant behaves similarly to $\|g\|_{p'}$, where $g \in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a standard Gaussian vector and $1/p + 1/p' = 1$. In contrast, for $p \in [1,2)$, the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constant aligns more closely with $\|g\|_2$. For networks with possibly nonzero biases, we obtain the same lower bounds without assumptions on the bias distributions. For symmetric bias distributions with bounded densities, we also derive high-probability upper bounds for the $\ell^p$-Lipschitz constants. For fixed sub-exponential bias distributions, these upper bounds differ from the lower bounds by a factor that has square-root dependence on the depth and logarithmic dependence on the width.
item.dc:creator: Sjoerd Dirksen, Patrick Finke, Paul Geuchen, Dominik St\"oger, Felix Voigtlaender

item.title: Non-linear Dirichlet Functionals: Markovianity, Locality, Invariance
item.description: arXiv:2510.02942v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present in a unified setting the foundations for a theory of non-linear Dirichlet functionals on Hilbert spaces. We prove known and new equivalences between non-linear semigroups, non-linear resolvents, non-linear generators, and their energy functionals, including a complete characterization of Markovianity. We introduce and characterize strong notions of invariance for general lower semicontinuous convex functionals, and notions of locality and strong locality for non-linear Dirichlet functionals. Contrary to many partial results in the literature, these characterizations are complete under minimal natural assumptions, and reduce to the classical ones in the bilinear case. Our definitions and proofs simplify and clarify the analogous facts in the linear theory, showing in particular that (the equality defining) locality is a saturation of (the inequality defining) Markovianity.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Brigati, Lorenzo Dello Schiavo

item.title: Rao-Blackwellized e-variables
item.description: arXiv:2512.16759v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that for any concave utility, the expected utility of an e-variable can only increase after conditioning on a sufficient statistic, echoing the classic Rao-Blackwell theorem. The simplest form of the result has a straightforward proof using Jensen's inequality, but we prove more sophisticated versions. We provide several applications of this insight, including a derivation of the log-optimal e-variable for testing the variance in a linear regression model.
item.dc:creator: Dante de Roos, Ben Chugg, Peter Gr\"unwald, Aaditya Ramdas

item.title: GRAFT-ATHENA: Self-Improving Agentic Teams for Autonomous Discovery and Evolutionary Numerical Algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2605.11117v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Language-model agents plan, execute, and evaluate scientific workflows. However, the problem--method relationships guiding their choices remain implicit, so plausible outputs can violate the assumptions of the scientific problem. We introduce Graph Reduction to Adaptive Factored Trees (GRAFT), which makes this problem-to-method map explicit as an expandable probabilistic structure of admissible problems, methods, and dependencies. Because this structure follows scientific semantics, knowledge from documentation, papers, and domain experts can be encoded, while factorization keeps the structure tractable. Semantic fingerprints of encoded problems measure their similarity, so expertise and experience guide related problems. GRAFT-guided workflows exceeded published expert baselines in physics-informed learning, recovered blood-rheology trends, predicted Apollo Command Module hypersonic loading within 1.8\% of experiment, and established machine-checked error bounds for regularized brain-flow reconstruction and a spectral physics-informed architecture. The representation retains evaluated outcomes and incorporates new methods, allowing scientific knowledge and experience to accumulate.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Toscano, Zhaojie Chai, George Em Karniadakis

item.title: Diffusion-Based Stochastic Operator Networks for Uncertainty Quantification in Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.17107v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a novel framework for uncertainty quantification of solution operators associated with stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs). Although SPDEs play a central role in modeling complex physical systems under uncertainty, their practical use typically requires specifying the magnitude and structure of model uncertainties that are often unknown and difficult to infer from noisy measurements. To address this challenge, we develop a stochastic operator-learning framework that learns directly from noisy data and outputs both a mean solution field and a quantification of uncertainty. The proposed method, namely the Stochastic Operator Network (SON), is constructed by combining the structure of the Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) with Stochastic Neural Networks (SNNs) to model stochasticity and enable probabilistic prediction. The training procedure is carried out by minimizing a Hamiltonian-type loss and optimizing the resulting objective using the Stochastic Maximum Principle. Numerical experiments on benchmark SPDEs under multiple uncertainty sources demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method in capturing solution structure and quantifying predictive uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Phuoc-Toan Huynh, Richard Archibald, Feng Bao

item.title: Ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2607.16832v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials, a convexity-enhanced subclass of G\aa{}rding polynomials whose G{\aa}rding components are recursively convex under partial differentiation. This class strictly contains real stable polynomials and, after translation and homogenization, lies in the Lorentzian class. Our main result is that ideal G{\aa}rding polynomials still admit a robust structure theory despite this additional convexity: they are preserved under polarization, satisfy natural closure properties, and support a linear preserver theory. A key contribution of this paper is a universal model for univariate G{\aa}rding polynomials, described by monotone root sequences and equivalently by volume polynomials of Pitman--Stanley polytopes. We establish quotient concavity, and Newton--Maclaurin type inequalities, which leads to the polarization theorem, and suggests further connections with convex geometry and Lorentzian polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fang, Biao Ma

item.title: Almost Sharp Equivalence between Approximate Message Passing and Low-Degree Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.06988v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp lower bound for growing-degree polynomial estimation in the symmetric rank-one matrix estimation problem. The observation is \[ \boldsymbol{Y}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \boldsymbol{\theta} \boldsymbol{\theta}^{\top}+\boldsymbol{W}, \] where the coordinates of $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ are independent with a common, fixed sub-Gaussian distribution $\pi_\Theta$ satisfying $\mathbb E[\Theta]\neq0$, and $\boldsymbol{W}$ is symmetric with independent standard Gaussian upper-triangular entries. For every such prior, we give an explicit finite-dimensional bound implying that every sequence of polynomial estimators of degree $D(n)=o(n^{1/60})$ has normalized mean-square error with limit inferior at least $\mathbb E[\Theta^2]-q_{\mathsf{amp}}$, the limiting error of Bayes approximate message passing (AMP). This extends the constant-degree equivalence of Montanari and Wein~\cite{montanari2025equivalence} to growing degree under the same prior assumptions. Combined with their polynomial approximation of fixed-iteration AMP, the bound identifies the exact limiting low-degree MMSE whenever $D(n)\to\infty$ within this range. It thereby answers the growing-degree AMP-equivalence question discussed in~\cite{wein2025computational, maleki2026high} for nonzero-mean sub-Gaussian priors in the stated degree range. We also obtain a moment-dependent finite-dimensional lower bound for any nonzero-mean prior with all moments finite. The proof bounds low-degree MMSE using \emph{conditional} joint cumulants and a refined application of Jensen's inequality. The conditional cumulants are defined using an auxiliary Gaussian channel $\boldsymbol{R}$ calibrated to the AMP fixed point. This retains signal dependence that is lost in unconditional cumulant bounds and produces the cancellations needed for quantitative control as the degree grows.
item.dc:creator: Zhangsong Li

item.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$-time FPRAS for the Permanent
item.description: arXiv:2609.20717v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an FPRAS for the permanent of an $n\times n$ $0/1$ matrix with running time $\widetilde O(n^3)$. Our algorithm extends to a strongly polynomial FPRAS for arbitrary nonnegative matrices with the same running-time bound (but in the unit-cost arithmetic model). Jerrum, Sinclair, and Vigoda (2004) gave the first FPRAS for the permanent of a nonnegative matrix. The running time was subsequently improved to $\widetilde{O}(n^7)$ by Bez\'akov\'a, \v{S}tefankovi\v{c}, Vazirani, and Vigoda (2008), and recently to $\widetilde{O}(n^6)$ by Chen, Vigoda, and Yang (2026). We introduce a multicommodity-flow bound inspired by electrical flows, replacing the usual path-length factor by routing energy. For the classical JSV chain with perfect-matching weights multiplied by $n^2$, we prove a relaxation-time bound of $O(n^3\log n)$ and obtain comparable bounds for estimating the stationary probabilities of having a specified pair of unmatched vertices. We use a separate chain on assignments to generate a warm start at any given temperature, avoiding the long initialization of the JSV chain. Finally, we replace the JSV chain with a new chain that uses only $n$ hole weights and speeds up hole-weight learning by a factor of $n$.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyu Chen, Heng Guo, Eric Vigoda, Xiongxin Yang

item.title: Manifold Hypothesis: Conditional Certificates and Consistent Intrinsic Dimension Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2609.21311v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study what noisy data can justify before a manifold and its intrinsic dimension are assumed. For repeated observations with independent isotropic Gaussian errors of unknown variance, we compose a support confidence event with a sound geometric verifier to certify a nearby smooth witness of arbitrary compact latent support. Whole-support inference requires an external lower mass condition; independent validation instead certifies proximity of probability mass. Separate all-scale hypotheses yield true-support structure and dimension recovery: a credited Reifenberg--Dini criterion and positive continuous density give local $C^1$ structure and consistent dimension estimation, while two-sided Ahlfors regularity and positive reach give quantitative covariance separation under the stated sampling and observation-transfer conditions. An exact-arithmetic implementation verifies restricted witness families. A further matrix check certifies linear coordinates on a geometrically verified affine span containing the witness and propagates approximation and decoding errors. This restricted construction neither implements the general minimal-dimension Whitney theorem nor infers exact manifold support from finite approximation. Executed torus and Julia-set experiments test the observation-to-witness-to-coordinate route, including singular-support controls. Dynamical systems and chaos are the primary application context; state-identification and finite-horizon prediction results are conditional on observation embeddings and transition validation. Takens reconstruction is an optional scalar-delay application requiring additional smoothness, dynamics and observable conditions. Image comparisons are auxiliary reconstruction diagnostics. The finite-data verifier establishes neither those dynamical conditions nor the all-scale geometric premises for true-dimension recovery.
item.dc:creator: U Jin Choi

item.title: Optimal discrepancy for triangles
item.description: arXiv:2610.00375v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every $n$-point set in the plane has a two-coloring with discrepancy $O(n^{1/4})$ for all triangles. This improves the previous bound $O(n^{1/4}\sqrt{\log n})$ and matches the classical lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Gleb Smirnov

item.title: Sharp Asymptotic Theory of Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Gaussian Processes with an RBF Kernel
item.description: arXiv:2610.10080v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Gaussian processes (GPs) are widely used across machine learning, spatial statistics, time-series analysis, optimization, Bayesian statistics, and scientific applications. A central component of a GP model is its kernel, which is typically specified through a parametric family. Among the most widely used choices is the radial basis function (RBF), also known as the squared exponential or Gaussian kernel, owing to its simple form, smoothness, and flexibility. In practice, the kernel parameters are routinely estimated by the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs), as implemented by standard GP software. Despite this widespread use, the asymptotic behavior of the MLEs remains poorly understood under fixed-domain asymptotics, even for the RBF kernel. The main difficulty arises from the increasingly strong dependence among densely sampled observations and the nonlinear dependence of the covariance matrix on the kernel parameters. In this paper, we address this gap by providing, to the best of our knowledge, the first complete asymptotic characterization of the joint MLE of the spatial variance, lengthscale, and nugget variance under fixed-domain asymptotics. We establish consistency, derive convergence rates for all three parameters, prove joint asymptotic normality, and show that these rates are minimax optimal.
item.dc:creator: Ameer Qaqish, Sudipto Banerjee, Didong Li
